headline: Biggest vert ask fell short; ankle rolled twice
narrative: This was billed as the biggest vert week of the build so far, plus recon of the high mid-course, and it landed a bit short of that ask. Almost all the climbing came from just two outings: a big Wednesday day and a Saturday night trail run over Puig Campana. Thursday, Friday and Sunday were blank. That's less a fitness problem than a scheduling one — two strong days can't fully stand in for a week's worth of steady loading, and the recon brief only got partly ticked off.

The Puig Campana run is also where the flags sit. The ankle rolled twice on the technical descent terrain — a new signal worth watching alongside the knee/quad tendon soreness that's been lingering, which oddly felt fine while actually hammering the downhills. Nothing that stopped the session, but two ankle rolls in one outing is worth noting rather than shrugging off.

Cumulatively the build is still on track for Costa Blanca, and a lopsided week like this one won't move that needle much. Next week is a deload — the job now is to bank recovery, let the ankle and tendon settle, and not chase the vert this week left on the table.
